7. Effect of Increased Tolls
Under the proposed Treaty, Panama will receive an annual payment from toll revenues of 30 cents per ton. The 30 cents will be adjusted periodically by the Wholesale Price Index of All Manufactured Goods in the U.S. to reflect changes in prices. In addition, Panama will also get a fixed sum of $10 million yearly and an additional $10 million per annum if Canal traffic and revenues permit.
It is not possible at this time to estimate what percentage increase above current tolls will be necessary to cover these payments. This will depend on such factors as
 the structure of the canal operation during the new Treaty, especially its operating cost requirements; and
 the short-term impact on Canal traffic of Alaskan oil shipments.
In view of these factors, the following table - showing the estimated effect on Canal traffic at toll increases of 25, 30 and 35% - is simply illustrative. It should be noted that in the event toll increases over the current levels are required, the impact on canal traffic (i.e., the amount of traffic diverted) should not exceed 10% in any single year.

Explanatory Note
-- Analysis of the sensitivity of Panama Canal traffic to substantial toll increases shows that Canal traffic losses traceable to a substantial toll increase will rise for about ten years and then level off.
